Chernyakhiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyr Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Chernyakhiv's Jewish community, first mentioned in 1629, was annihilated during the 1648 Khmelnytsky Uprising and left unmentioned again for over 70 years, not resurfacing in records until 1721. It grew to nearly half the town's population by 1897, survived Civil War-era pogroms, and was largely destroyed when German forces killed most of its remaining members in the second half of 1941. The cemetery, established by the early 20th century, lost its western section during the war — later relocated to the now-fenced eastern part — and has since been restored twice, in 1994 and 2012, with two memorials honoring the Shoah's victims.
